primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_j(t)': 'Attention index of rusher j at time t, normalized between 0 and 1', 't': 'Time in seconds'}

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in adapting a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) originally developed for basketball to the domain of American football. The model processes high-dimensional spatio-temporal tracking data to produce frame-by-frame probabilistic assignments of each pass blocker to a rusher. This allows for a continuous-time evaluation of blocking performance, moving beyond binary outcomes like sacks or hurries. The probabilistic nature enables nuanced modeling of player interactions, where a rusher may command partial attention from multiple blockers simultaneously. The derived block-shedding survival metric captures how long a blocker remains effective, while the rusher attention quantification measures defensive influence. These primitives form a dual framework: one for evaluating individual blocker efficacy and another for assessing defensive pressure distribution. Failure modes include data gaps, misalignment of tracking systems, or oversimplification of complex human decision-making. The model’s robustness hinges on accurate tracking and consistent application of the HMM framework across varying game states.
